purpose: Localize why the frozen five-neural/six-formula hybrid is slower than an all-formula block after symmetric Inductor compilation. This is a diagnostic decomposition, not a new Gate D promotion test.
interpretation: The core contrast identifies whether the learned five-channel module itself costs more than five formulas. Gate-only and full contrasts test fusion/assembly and current-head overhead. Tail/current timings are standalone diagnostics; component times are not additive because compiler fusion differs across compositions. CUDA profiler kernel counts and top kernel names are supportive, not a substitute for paired events.
decision: No Task29 authorization or Gate D reclassification. Select the next architectural hypothesis only from the measured bottleneck and preserve the compiled NO-GO.
